::: callout-note
#### Estimators are random variables

When an estimator is applied to random variables $\dsn{X}$
rather than to their observed values,
the result $\hparam(\dsn{X})$ is also a random variable.
:::

::: callout-note
#### Notation for estimators

Estimators are often symbolized by placing a hat over the symbol of the
corresponding estimand; for example, $\hparam$.
The [notation choices page](https://morrison-lab.github.io/macros/notation-choices.html#sec-estimand-estimator-symbols)
gives our convention and the alternatives.

Usually, their dependence on the data is implicit:

$$\hparam \eqdef \hparam(\dsn{x})$$

:::
